title: A Rapid and Chemical-free Hemoglobin Assay with Photothermal Angular Light Scattering
protocol: Mount an empty micro-capillary tube on a capillary tube fixture.
Anchor a 650 nm laser pointer to illuminate the capillary tube.
Ensure the probe beam is larger than the capillary tube.
Place a screen behind the capillary tube to observe the angular periodic pattern.
Remove any lenses in a webcam to directly capture the scattering pattern.
Position the webcam at an angle of 25-35° relative to the probe beam direction.
Observe the angular periodic pattern in the middle of the image sensor.
Position a 532-nm PT excitation light source to illuminate the capillary tube.
Ensure the PT excitation light overlaps with the probe beam on the capillary tube.
Use the highest optical power of the employed PT excitation light source.
Place a long-pass filter in front of the detector to block the 532-nm light.
Install an optical chopper in the path of the PT excitation light before illuminating the capillary tube.
Draw 6 ml of fresh whole blood in ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid blood sampling tubes.
Mix the blood samples well.
Measure the blood samples using the PT-AS sensor within 24 hours of extraction.
Load a micro-capillary tube with a blood sample through capillary action by placing the tube into the blood sample.
Mount the capillary tube at the designated position in the fixture.
Turn on the 650 nm probe laser to illuminate the blood-loaded micro-capillary tube.
Turn on the 532-nm PT excitation laser to illuminate the tube.
Set the modulation frequency using the control knob in the chopper control box.
Run the optical chopper to modulate the intensity of the PT excitation light at 2 Hz.
Record the fluctuating scattering pattern via the webcam for 5 sec in MPEG-4 (mp4) format.
Load the video file to extract the images.
For each image, obtain the averaged scattering pattern by computing the mean of the pixel values along the vertical direction.
Evaluate the Fourier transform of the averaged scattering pattern.
Compute the phase at the peak spatial frequency.
Perform these operations for all frames of all recorded images.
Using the phase values obtained from all images, plot the temporal phase fluctuation.
Take the Fourier transform of the phase fluctuation in the time domain.
Obtain the magnitude at the modulation frequency.
Measure [Hb] of a blood sample by converting its PT-AS signal into the corresponding [Hb] using the calibration curve.
Prepare blood samples having [Hb] values uniformly distributed in the detection range of the PT-AS sensor.
Quantify the [Hb] values of the samples using a reference hematology analyzer.
Measure the PT-AS signals of the samples.
Derive a calibration curve relating [Hb] to the PT-AS signal by performing a linear least squares fit.
Use MATLAB code to perform the linear fit.
